claim: People prefer, and extract as the 'good part' of an analogy, facts embedded in a shared causal system over equally matching isolated facts (systematicity as selection constraint).
agent_test: Give the agent two candidate transfers (one inside the shared causal chain, one isolated). Compare accuracy of picking the supported one with and without a code-side systematicity score at equal tokens.

claim: Soundness judgments follow shared higher-order relational structure, while memory retrieval follows surface similarity; the two orders are uncorrelated (r(52)=.15). Re-opened: soundness 4.40 vs 2.80 vs 2.74; retrieval .78 surface, .44 analogy, .25 first-order (Exp 1); across three studies surface .78/.53/.52 vs analogy .44/.12/.07.
agent_test: Retrieval of past cases by embedding similarity will return surface twins. Test: embedding-only retrieval vs embedding then structural re-rank; measure the share of retrieved cases that actually help.
audit_note: Numbers all match Gentner Rattermann Forbus 1993 (soundness 4.40/2.80/2.74, retrieval .78/.44/.25, r(52)=.15, three-study .78/.53/.52 vs .44/.12/.07); evidence is one paper (plus a same-lab review).

claim: Two-stage retrieval (cheap surface filter, then structural scoring of a few candidates) reproduces the human pattern and runs about two orders of magnitude faster than the constraint-satisfaction rival ARCS.
agent_test: Compare MAC/FAC-style two-stage case retrieval with one-stage embedding retrieval at equal token budget.

claim: The SME score favours the textbook mapping by structure alone: heat/water top gmap 5.99 (re-confirmed in the paper), solar system/atom 6.03 vs spurious 1.87 (re-confirmed).
agent_test: Check that a code scorer over LLM-written relation lists ranks the correct mapping first on a small labelled set (water/heat, atom/solar system, plus our own).
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: SME is sensitive to how the descriptions are written. Flat, relation-poor descriptions are slow and brittle; adding higher-order structure cut one run from 53 minutes to 34 seconds (re-confirmed). Mismatched abstraction levels break matching.
agent_test: Vary the abstraction level of the LLM-written relation lists (flat vs causal chain) and measure mapping accuracy.

claim: SME's greedy merge keeps mapping construction polynomial (O(n^2 log n)); in an early 1990 test of a simple version of greedy merge on 56 analogies, it produced the same best mapping as exhaustive merge in 52 (93%), and failed in 4 where many large kernels conflicted (reported in Forbus et al. 2017).
agent_test: Implement greedy merge in code. Check accuracy parity with exhaustive search on our small descriptions.
audit_note: Forbus et al. 2017 gives O(n^2 log n) and the 52 of 56 (93%) figure, but it is a 1990 test (Forbus and Oblinger) of a simple early version of greedy merge, not the current multi-mapping version; the two cited SME sources are the same paper and the SMTB paper does not report it.
claim_before_audit: Greedy merge keeps SME polynomial (O(n^2 log n)) and finds the same best mapping as exhaustive merge in 52 of 56 test analogies (93%).

claim: Inference gating: a candidate inference is more credible when more of the mapping supports it (support score) and less when it extrapolates far; this reproduced human inductive-strength orderings in simulation and picked the best advice in a small coaching prototype.
agent_test: Accept a transferred step only if its support score passes a threshold; compare the error rate of transferred steps against ungated transfer.

claim: Comparing two cases side by side (analogical encoding) gives more schema formation and transfer than studying them separately: 47% vs 6% baseline (Exp 1, N=48, re-confirmed), 48% vs 19% (Exp 2, N=128, re-confirmed); face-to-face negotiation 90% guided vs 70% comparison (re-confirmed).
agent_test: Give the agent two solved cases in one prompt with an explicit compare step vs the same two cases listed separately; measure solve rate on a third case.
audit_note: Numbers match Gentner Loewenstein Thompson 2003 (47% vs 6% N=48; 48% vs 19% N=128; 90/70/55/37 face-to-face); the 47% is guided-analogy training, not plain side-by-side comparison, and both sources share authors.

claim: Inert knowledge: people given a prior case rarely use it unprompted (3 of 16 used the principle; about 10% solve Duncker's problem unaided, second-hand).
agent_test: Test whether the agent uses a relevant case it was given without being told to, vs when told to compare.
audit_note: 3 of 16 (19%) used the tradeoff principle, 2 before and 1 after a recall question; the 10% Duncker figure is second-hand as stated.

claim: Rating similarity first pushes people to map by relations and to resolve cross-mapped objects relationally (.69 vs .42 one-shot).
agent_test: Require the agent to write what is shared before mapping; compare cross-mapped-object error.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Under very short deadlines metaphor direction effects vanish and similarity is judged on local matches; relational alignment needs time.
agent_test: Low priority. Implies a cheap first pass is surface-driven, so force a second relational pass.

claim: SME-based models reproduce human performance on Raven's: 56/60, 75th percentile of 1993 US adult norms; human college sample 54/60 (61st percentile); model errors fall on hard items; regressions explain .63 and .67 of item variance. Re-opened and confirmed (the 41st percentile figure in the paper belongs to a different model, 50/60).
agent_test: Not directly testable on a text agent. Ceiling evidence that explicit structure mapping plus re-representation works on relational problems.
audit_note: Lovett and Forbus 2017: 56/60 = 75th percentile (1993 norms), college sample 54/60 = 61st percentile, regressions .63 and .67; the 41st percentile figure belongs to a different (50/60) model.

claim: A mapper without semantic abstraction fails: embedding-based structural mapping on raw event phrases scores below chance (0.17 vs 0.25 MCQ; 0.24 vs 0.50 ARN far). Adding LLM abstraction lifts MCQ to 0.46 (Qwen) and 0.45 (Llama). Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Ablate the abstraction step of our O7: raw relation lists vs abstracted lists feeding the same code scorer.

claim: A hybrid LLM-then-structural-mapper beats the LLM alone on far analogies for Llama (0.46 vs 0.42) but not Qwen (0.47 vs 0.52 zero-shot), and loses on near analogies (Qwen CoT 0.79 vs 0.69). Mixed, one paper.
agent_test: Route by distance: plain similarity for near cases, structural step only when surface overlap is low; compare against always-on.

claim: LLMs are far below humans when surface similarity conflicts with relational structure: ARN far analogies 39.6% (chance 50%) vs humans 94.1%; far analogy vs near distractor 33.9% even when prompted for system mappings. SBERT alone gets 77.9% on near. Re-opened and confirmed (2023 zero-shot models).
agent_test: Build far-analogy vs surface-distractor items; compare plain prompt, 'use relations' prompt, and code-side structure scoring at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: StoryAnalogy: best LLM trails humans by 37.7 points on multiple choice (human 85.7%, ChatGPT about 30%, davinci-003 37.1%, SME-style method 44.9%).
agent_test: Same test as above on story-level items.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: On the Gentner et al. 1993 story analogies, GPT-3 was worse than students (OR=.37, p=.0003; far analogy not above chance, p=.065), while GPT-4 reached significance on far (27 of 36 comparisons, two-sided binomial p=.0039); GPT-4 is correct more often when the right answer is listed first (Lewis and Mitchell: 1.00 vs .72). Item-level work (Inani et al.) finds a BERT embedding model's item difficulty does not track human difficulty (r=-.03, p=.899).
agent_test: Use these 18 story triples as a small sanity test with answer order shuffled (GPT-4 reported 89% first vs 61% second).
audit_note: Webb numbers (OR=0.37 p=.0003; GPT-3 far p=.065; GPT-4 far two-sided binomial p=.0039) are right, but p=.0039 corresponds to 27 of 36 correct (18 stories x 2 orders; Lewis and Mitchell list Webb's GPT-4 total as 27/36), not 8 of 8 (8/8 two-sided is .0078); also the r=-.032 in Inani et al. is between humans and a BERT sentence-embedding model, not LLM errors.
claim_before_audit: On the Gentner et al. 1993 story analogies, GPT-3 was worse than students (OR=.37, p=.0003; far analogy not above chance, p=.065), while GPT-4 reached significance on far (p=.0039). Item counts per condition are small (p=.0039 equals 8 of 8 correct under a two-sided binomial). Later item-level work finds LLM errors do not track human difficulty (r=-.03).

claim: Letter-string analogy: GPT-3 beat students on the original task (Webb) but counterfactual alphabets show a large drop for models (humans .753 vs GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452 in Lewis and Mitchell; confirmed on re-open, table text is garbled) while humans stay high.
agent_test: Do not treat letter-string scores as evidence of mapping skill. Use counterfactual variants as a control.
audit_note: Webb (letter strings OR=1.76, p=6.3e-5), Lewis and Mitchell (humans .753, GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452 over counterfactual sets; Table 2 text garbled but order consistent) and Hodel and West all agree.

claim: The counterfactual letter-string failure is partly an exact-counting failure: GPT-4 with code execution solved shuffled-alphabet problems at about human level, without code it failed (authors' own reply; one group). (Update: the PNAS Nexus version reports the same result, still by the same authors. Free-form Python did not help text input on ConceptARC in an outside lab, so the code gain looks specific to exact counting.)
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool for exact matching and counting vs none; measure on counterfactual relational items.

claim: Models are not robust across symbol alphabets: GPT-4o .85 Latin to .48 Symbol, Llama-405B .79 to .27, vs adults .88 to .89 and children .62 to .67.
agent_test: Rename entities and relation labels in test items; measure invariance of the mapping output.
audit_note: Stevenson et al. table matches (adults .88/.91/.89, children .62/.66/.67, GPT-4o .85/.63/.48, Llama-405B .79/.74/.27 for Latin/Greek/Symbol).

claim: Analogical prompting (model writes its own related problems) improves on 0-shot CoT in the original paper (GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.8 to 77.8; MATH 33.9 to 37.3; text-davinci-003 GSM8K 14.8 to 61.0 vs 0-shot). Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Baseline arm for any analogical step.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The gain from self-generated 'analogous' examples does not need relevance: on math, irrelevant or N/A examples match or beat relevant ones (GSM8K relevant 71.5 vs N/A 75.5, Randomdiff 76.3; MATH 33.3 vs 36.1). Correctness of the example matters. On BBH relevant examples did win on average. Re-opened and confirmed. Baselines differ from Yasunaga (their relevant 71.5 vs 77.8), so the two are not like for like.
agent_test: Always include a random-correct-example control arm when crediting a gain to analogy.

claim: Thought propagation (solve analogous problems, reuse their solutions) improves optimal rate on shortest path (GPT-3.5 0.65 vs IO 0.33) and ALFWorld, with no control for random-example effects.
agent_test: Add an irrelevant-solved-problem control.

claim: LLM-built relation sets plus a structural mapper (FAME) map word-level domains well (81.2% on classical 2x2, 77.8% perfect on extended vs 13.1% chance), but plain GPT-3.5 matches it on web-available 2x2 problems (92/80%) and falls on larger unseen ones (44-58% vs 77.8%). Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Test on larger unseen mapping problems (3+ entities), where code-side one-to-one search should help most.

claim: Relation extraction from corpus statistics alone can reach human level on word mapping (LRME 91.5% vs humans 87.6% on 20 problems, N=22 humans, not significantly different).
agent_test: Low priority. Suggests relation quality, not search, is the bottleneck.

claim: In the sources read, no study measures whether an SME-style structural score computed from LLM-written relation lists predicts that a transferred step helps an agent at matched tokens. (Gap search 2026-10: still none found, though the search was rate-limited.)
agent_test: The core experiment to run: score vs benefit of the transferred step.

claim: Internal representations hold relational information in mid layers; patching hidden states repairs up to 38.4% of failed cases, suggesting a second bottleneck is applying relations to new entities.
agent_test: Not testable in a scaffold.

claim: A formal check of structure-mapping constraints scores LLMs low (functional/structural ratio LLMs 0.109 vs SME 0.606); the survey finds no strong evidence for systematicity or explicit inferential projection in LLMs.
agent_test: Survey judgement, not an experiment. Do not rely on it.

claim: GPT-4 (0613) on the 18 Webb story analogies is biased by answer position (correct first 1.00, second 0.72; Webb's data 0.89 vs 0.61) and drops on paraphrase (0.86 to 0.72), while humans show no position bias (0.78 both). Not tested on current models; no test of shuffling or voting.
agent_test: Pick the source case from a shuffled candidate list, three orders, majority vote. Compare with a single fixed order on a current model.

claim: LLM extraction of relations is unstable between runs, and worse for long input: Jaccard overlap with run 1 is about 0.55 for atomic facts and about 0.21 for whole paragraphs (gpt-4.1, 3 runs). This is a proxy; relation lists for cases were not measured.
agent_test: Extract relation lists three times per case; measure overlap; keep only relations seen in at least two runs; check whether mapping scores steady.

claim: On flat first-order relation lists SME has no higher-order signal and reduces to greedy merging. SMTB, a bounded-search mapper, solved the 5,845-pair SME corpus 5 to 15 times faster (70.95 s vs 5.97 s greedy) with mappings scoring about 22% higher on the authors' scale. Authors' own benchmark.
agent_test: Use plain greedy one-to-one merge in code; compare with a bounded search on LLM-written lists to see if the extra score gives any gain in downstream help.

claim: On Raven-style analogy rules, reasoning models fell to near chance (o3-mini 86.6% to 17.0%, R1 80.6% to 23.2%; chance 12.5%) when wide value ranges and noisy perception were combined; a neuro-symbolic solver fell only from 98.6% to 88.0%. Reasoning models used 4,486 to 19,449 tokens per item.
agent_test: Add noise to the relation lists (drop or swap 10-30% of relations). Measure score drop for code mapping vs model-only comparison.

claim: Free-form Python access did not raise text-input accuracy on ConceptARC for o3 (77.1 to 75.6), Claude Sonnet 4 (60.2 to 55.0) or Gemini 2.5 Pro (66.0 to 60.4). About 27% of correct text answers by o3 and Gemini (19% Claude, 7% humans) came from a wrong or unintended rule.
agent_test: Check transferred steps for the right reason, not just the right final answer.

claim: Giving frontier models the text of the three solutions from an earlier same-structure environment helped little: only Gemini 3 Flash showed significant transfer (9.08 to 7.33 attempts); GPT-5.2 did not gain (15.77 to 17.43); humans gained 33% (d=0.71).
agent_test: A transferred step must be re-checked in the new setting before it is trusted.

claim: Anchoring the search on a structure mapping between a worked example and a new problem put the intended procedure first for 86.7% of 120 numeric changes vs 26.7% for random order, with 93.8% fewer combinations tested (simulation, no LLM, random baseline).
agent_test: Order candidate inferences by their link to the mapped region and test whether the first accepted one is right more often than a model-ordered list.

claim: A one-to-one assignment (greedy or Kuhn-Munkres) over similarity scores between concept pairs beat picking the most similar concept per item on 400 scientific analogies (SCAR); LLM system-level accuracy trailed humans (GPT-4 about 65-69 vs 86).
agent_test: Enforce one-to-one in code on LLM-proposed pairs.

claim: Not found in the sources read (search was rate-limited): any test of structural score predicting benefit at matched tokens; token cost of a mapping step vs side-by-side cases; LLM analogical encoding with a random-correct-case control; support-threshold gating in a model; preregistered or many-lab replication of the classic human results.
agent_test: Run these as our own tests.
